title: Jennifer Lawrence's New Movie Die My Love — Everything We Know
excerpt: Jennifer Lawrence reunites with Robert Pattinson in Die My Love, a psychological drama from Lynne Ramsay. Cast, plot, and what to expect.
author: StarScoop Daily Staff
imageAlt: Die My Love official backdrop — Jennifer Lawrence's new movie with Robert Pattinson
metaDescription: Jennifer Lawrence's new movie Die My Love — full cast, plot, Robert Pattinson, director Lynne Ramsay, and everything confirmed so far.
content:
Jennifer Lawrence's new movie is not a comeback vehicle or a franchise play. It's Die My Love — a psychological drama that sounds genuinely punishing, directed by one of the most uncompromising filmmakers working today.

She stars opposite Robert Pattinson, with Sissy Spacek, LaKeith Stanfield and Nick Nolte in support. Here's everything confirmed.

What Die My Love Is About

The setup is deceptively simple. After inheriting a remote Montana house, Jackson moves there from New York with his partner Grace, and the couple soon welcome a child.

Then it curdles. As Jackson becomes increasingly absent and rural isolation sets in, Grace struggles with loneliness, creative frustration, and unresolved emotional wounds. What starts as an attempt at renewal turns into an intense psychological descent — one that strains the relationship and exposes the fragile balance between love, identity, and motherhood.

That last phrase is the key to the whole film. This is a story about postpartum isolation and the erasure of a woman's sense of self, told without the softening a studio would normally insist on.

Why Lynne Ramsay Directing Changes Everything

Lynne Ramsay is the reason to pay attention here.

Ramsay directed We Need to Talk About Kevin and You Were Never Really Here — films that treat psychological damage as something to be inhabited rather than explained. She works in silence, texture and implication. Her films do not offer comfort, and they do not resolve neatly.

She also makes films rarely, which means each one arrives with genuine weight. Pairing her with Lawrence on material about maternal breakdown is about as far from a safe commercial choice as a major-name actor can make.

For Lawrence specifically, this is the continuation of a deliberate pattern. Post-Hunger Games, she has repeatedly chosen difficult, director-driven work over franchise security — and this is the most extreme version of that instinct so far.

The Cast — Lawrence and Pattinson Together

The confirmed cast:

  • Jennifer Lawrence as Grace
  • Robert Pattinson as Jackson
  • Sissy Spacek
  • LaKeith Stanfield
  • Nick Nolte
  • Gabrielle Rose, Clare Coulter, Sarah Lind

Lawrence and Pattinson is the pairing that will sell tickets, and it's a smart one. Both came out of enormous young-adult franchises — The Hunger Games and Twilight — and both spent the years afterward systematically working with difficult auteurs to dismantle that association. Pattinson did it with the Safdie brothers, Claire Denis and Robert Eggers. Lawrence did it with Darren Aronofsky and Adam McKay.

Casting them opposite each other in a Lynne Ramsay film is almost a thesis statement about that shared career arc.

Sissy Spacek in support is the detail cinephiles will notice. She built her career on Carrie and Badlands — films about young women unravelling. Her presence in a story about maternal collapse reads as deliberate.

Release Date — What's Confirmed

A firm wide release date has not been locked publicly. Films in this category — auteur-driven, awards-positioned, difficult subject matter — typically follow a festival-first strategy, premiering at Cannes, Venice or Telluride before a limited autumn rollout and an expansion if the reviews land.

Expect that pattern here rather than a conventional wide opening. Reportedly the film has been positioned for an awards-season window, which would fit both Ramsay's profile and the subject matter.

Should You Watch It?

Be honest with yourself about what this is. Die My Love is not a date-night film and it is not going to be a fun two hours. Ramsay does not make films that let you off.

But if you want to see what Jennifer Lawrence can actually do with material that doesn't protect her — the kind of performance that Winter's Bone announced before the franchise years — this is the one to watch for.
